Presented here are fabrication techniques and integrated circuit (IC) designs. These techniques allow a gate contact to be created on a gate that sits above—or nearby—the active region of a field effect transistor (FET). They also guard against short circuits that could occur between the gate contact and the metal plugs positioned on source/drain regions, as well as between the gate and the source/drain contacts leading to those metal plugs.

The process begins by building a gate, complete with a dielectric cap and dielectric sidewall spacer, atop the channel region of a FET. Following this, metal plugs featuring their own supplementary dielectric caps are placed on the FET's source/drain regions. This arrangement positions the dielectric sidewall spacer both between the gate and the metal plugs, and between the dielectric cap and the supplementary dielectric caps.

Crucially, the dielectric cap, the dielectric sidewall spacer, and the supplementary dielectric caps are made from distinct materials, chosen specifically because they can be etched selectively. This selective etchability means that even if a contact opening intended for the gate becomes misaligned, no metal plugs will be inadvertently exposed—and the same protection applies in reverse.

# Gate Contact Formation Over Active Regions in Field Effect Transistors

## Overview

The disclosed methods and integrated circuit structures enable the formation of a gate contact on a gate positioned above or near the active region of a field effect transistor (FET). This capability represents a significant advancement in semiconductor fabrication, as it allows for more compact device layouts and improved area efficiency by enabling gate contacts to be placed directly over active regions rather than requiring dedicated contact areas outside the active region.

## Protection Against Electrical Shorts

A key advantage of this design is its robust protection against unintended electrical shorts. Specifically, the structure guards against electrical shorts that could otherwise occur between the gate contact and the metal plugs formed on the source/drain regions. Additionally, it provides protection against shorts between the gate and the source/drain contacts. This dual protection is critical for maintaining device reliability and ensuring proper isolation between the various conductive elements within the transistor.

## Structural Configuration

The integrated circuit structure is built around a carefully engineered arrangement of components. A gate, featuring both a dielectric cap and a dielectric sidewall spacer, is formed on the channel region of the FET. In parallel, metal plugs are formed on the source/drain regions, and these plugs are provided with their own additional dielectric caps. This configuration ensures that each conductive element is appropriately insulated by dielectric materials.

## Spatial Arrangement of Dielectric Elements

The dielectric sidewall spacer plays a central role in the overall design by serving as an insulating barrier at two critical interfaces. First, it is positioned between the gate and the metal plugs, providing lateral separation between these conductive structures. Second, it is positioned between the dielectric cap of the gate and the additional dielectric caps of the metal plugs. This strategic positioning ensures comprehensive electrical isolation throughout the structure.

## Material Selection and Etch Selectivity

A crucial feature of the disclosed design is the deliberate selection of materials for the dielectric components. The dielectric cap, the sidewall spacer, and the additional caps are each made of different materials that are selectively etchable relative to one another. This difference in etch characteristics is what enables the process to tolerate misalignment during the formation of the contact opening. As a result, even if the contact opening is not perfectly aligned, the selective etching properties prevent any of the metal plugs from being inadvertently exposed. This tolerance for misalignment greatly enhances the manufacturability and yield of the device while preserving the integrity of the electrical isolation.

# Gate Contact Formation Over Active Region with Enhanced Short-Circuit Protection

## Field of the Invention

The present disclosure relates generally to the fabrication of integrated circuit structures, and more particularly to methods and structures for forming a gate contact above the active region of a field effect transistor (FET) while preventing electrical shorts between the gate contact and adjacent source/drain metal plugs.

## Background

As integrated circuit devices continue to scale to ever-smaller dimensions, the spacing between transistor features has diminished significantly. In advanced transistor architectures, the gate structure and the source/drain contacts are positioned in close proximity to one another. Conventionally, gate contacts have been formed over isolation regions rather than directly over the active region of the transistor, in part to avoid the risk of inadvertently shorting the gate contact to the neighboring source/drain metal plugs.

However, routing the gate contact over the isolation region consumes valuable chip area and imposes layout constraints that limit device density. Forming the gate contact directly above the active region would offer substantial area savings and greater design flexibility, but doing so introduces a significant reliability challenge: any misalignment of the contact opening during patterning may expose an adjacent source/drain metal plug, creating an unintended electrical short between the gate and the source/drain regions. Given the tight tolerances involved, even minor lithographic misalignment can compromise device functionality and yield.

## Summary of the Invention

Methods and integrated circuit structures are disclosed for forming a gate contact above the active region of a field effect transistor while protecting against shorts between the gate contact and the source/drain metal plugs. This protection is achieved through a self-aligned architecture in which the gate structure is provided with a dielectric cap and a sidewall spacer, while the source/drain metal plugs are provided with additional dielectric caps formed from materials that are selectively etchable relative to the surrounding dielectrics.

The use of dielectric materials having differing etch selectivities is central to the approach. By selecting the gate cap, the sidewall spacer, and the metal plug caps from materials that etch at substantially different rates under a given etch chemistry, the contact opening can be etched down to the gate while the protective caps over the adjacent metal plugs remain substantially intact. In this way, the etch process is inherently self-aligned: the opening is directed toward the gate conductor without removing the protective dielectric that shields the neighboring metal plugs.

## Detailed Description

In a representative embodiment, a field effect transistor is formed on a semiconductor substrate, comprising a gate structure disposed over a channel region and source/drain regions located on opposing sides of the gate. The gate structure includes a gate conductor capped by a dielectric gate cap and laterally bounded by dielectric sidewall spacers. Source/drain metal plugs are formed in contact with the source/drain regions, and each such plug is topped with an additional dielectric cap.

The dielectric gate cap, the sidewall spacers, and the metal plug caps are composed of different dielectric materials, each chosen so that at least one may be etched selectively with respect to the others. For example, the gate cap may comprise one dielectric material, the metal plug caps a second material, and the sidewall spacers a third material, such that an etchant used to open the contact to the gate removes the gate cap while leaving the metal plug caps and sidewall spacers largely unaffected.

To form the gate contact, a contact opening is patterned in an overlying interlayer dielectric above the gate. Because the metal plug caps are resistant to the etch chemistry used to open the contact to the gate, the opening may be intentionally or unintentionally offset toward one of the adjacent source/drain plugs without exposing the underlying metal. The selectively etchable caps thus absorb the effects of any misalignment, ensuring that the conductive gate contact material, once deposited, makes electrical connection only to the gate conductor and not to the source/drain plugs.

## Advantages

This approach provides several important benefits. First, it enables misalignment tolerance of the contact opening relative to the gate without risking exposure of any adjacent metal plugs, and conversely protects the gate from exposure when contacts are formed to the source/drain plugs. Second, by permitting the gate contact to be placed directly over the active region rather than over the isolation region, the disclosed structure achieves significant area savings and greater layout flexibility. Finally, the self-aligned, etch-selective scheme significantly improves the reliability and manufacturing yield of gate contact formation in closely spaced transistor architectures, where conventional alignment margins are insufficient to reliably prevent gate-to-source/drain shorts.

Taken together, these methods and structures allow for robust, high-density integration of field effect transistors while maintaining the electrical integrity of the gate and source/drain connections.

# The Disclosed FET: Structure and Applications

## Overview

The disclosed FET (Field-Effect Transistor) represents a fundamental building block of modern electronic systems. As a voltage-controlled semiconductor device, the disclosed FET regulates current flow through a channel by applying an electric field via its gate terminal. This document outlines the primary characteristics, operating principles, and practical applications of the technology.

## Structure and Operation

The disclosed FET consists of three main terminals: the source, the drain, and the gate. In operation, the voltage applied to the gate creates an electric field that modulates the conductivity of the channel between the source and drain. Because the gate is electrically isolated from the channel, the disclosed FET draws virtually no input current, resulting in extremely high input impedance.

Depending on the configuration, the disclosed FET may be classified as either:

- **JFET (Junction Field-Effect Transistor)** — using a reverse-biased p-n junction to control the channel.
- **MOSFET (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor FET)** — using an insulated gate separated by an oxide layer.

## Advantages

The disclosed FET offers several notable benefits over bipolar alternatives:

1. **High input impedance**, minimizing loading effects on preceding circuit stages.
2. **Low power consumption**, making it ideal for battery-operated devices.
3. **Excellent scalability**, enabling billions of transistors on a single integrated circuit.
4. **Thermal stability**, reducing the risk of thermal runaway.

## Applications

The disclosed FET has been widely adopted across numerous fields. In digital electronics, it forms the basis of logic gates, memory cells, and microprocessors. In analog systems, the disclosed FET is employed in amplifiers, signal switches, and voltage regulators. Power variants of the disclosed FET are essential in motor control, power supplies, and electric vehicle systems.

## Conclusion

The disclosed FET remains an indispensable component in contemporary electronics. Its versatility, efficiency, and scalability ensure that the disclosed FET will continue to play a central role in the ongoing advancement of semiconductor technology.

Methods and integrated circuit (IC) structures are provided for forming a gate contact over an active region of a field-effect transistor (FET) while preventing electrical shorts between the gate contact and adjacent source/drain metal plugs. In one aspect, an IC structure includes a gate structure disposed over a semiconductor substrate, source/drain regions adjacent the gate structure, and source/drain metal plugs electrically coupled to the source/drain regions. A dielectric cap comprising a first dielectric material is formed over the source/drain metal plugs, and a gate cap comprising a second dielectric material, having an etch selectivity different from the first dielectric material, is formed over the gate structure. A gate contact opening is patterned through the gate cap using a selective etch process that removes the second dielectric material while substantially preserving the dielectric cap over the source/drain metal plugs, thereby providing a self-aligned gate contact. A conductive material is deposited within the gate contact opening to form the gate contact in electrical connection with the gate structure. The differential etch selectivity between the gate cap and the source/drain dielectric caps enables the gate contact to be positioned over the active region with reduced spacing tolerances while maintaining electrical isolation from the source/drain metal plugs, improving device density and reliability. # Patent Abstract

## Self-Aligned Gate Contact Process Using Selectively Etchable Dielectric Caps and Sidewall Spacers

A semiconductor fabrication method and structure enabling self-aligned gate contact formation with enhanced tolerance to contact opening misalignment. The process comprises forming a plurality of gate structures on a substrate, each gate structure including a conductive gate electrode capped with a dielectric cap layer comprising a first dielectric material. Sidewall spacers comprising a second dielectric material are disposed along vertical surfaces of the gate structures, wherein the first dielectric material and the second dielectric material exhibit etch selectivity relative to one another and relative to an interlayer dielectric (ILD) comprising a third material. Metal source/drain contact plugs are formed within the ILD adjacent the gate structures and are self-aligned by the sidewall spacers.

A gate contact opening is subsequently patterned and etched through the dielectric cap layer to expose an upper surface of the gate electrode. Due to the etch selectivity among the dielectric cap, the sidewall spacers, and the surrounding ILD, the gate contact opening may be positioned with lateral misalignment relative to the underlying gate electrode without etching through the sidewall spacers or exposing the adjacent metal contact plugs. The dielectric cap and sidewall spacers thereby function as an etch-resistant containment structure that protects the metal plugs from electrical shorting to the gate contact.

The disclosed process relaxes lithographic overlay and critical dimension requirements, reduces the risk of gate-to-source/drain shorts, and enables tighter contacted gate pitch scaling in advanced integrated circuit devices.

# Patent Abstract

## Selectively Etchable Dielectric Structures for Prevention of Gate-to-Source/Drain Contact Shorts in Field Effect Transistors

**ABSTRACT**

A semiconductor device structure and method of fabrication are disclosed for preventing electrical shorts between a gate electrode and source/drain contacts in a field effect transistor (FET). The structure comprises a gate stack disposed over a semiconductor substrate, the gate stack including a gate conductor encapsulated by a first dielectric material having a first etch selectivity. A second dielectric material having a second etch selectivity, distinct from the first etch selectivity, is disposed adjacent to the source/drain regions to define contact trench regions. The differential etch selectivity between the first and second dielectric materials enables formation of self-aligned source/drain contact openings while preserving dielectric integrity along gate sidewalls and gate cap regions.

In accordance with the disclosed method, a self-aligned contact (SAC) etch process is performed wherein the second dielectric material is selectively removed at a substantially higher etch rate relative to the first dielectric material, thereby exposing the underlying source/drain regions without eroding the protective dielectric encapsulating the gate conductor. The first dielectric material, which may comprise silicon nitride, silicon carbonitride, or a low-k dielectric, functions as an etch stop and insulating barrier that maintains a predetermined minimum spacing between the conductive contact metallization and the gate conductor. This configuration substantially reduces the risk of gate-to-source/drain shorting arising from contact-to-gate misalignment, particularly at reduced device pitches.

The resulting transistor structure exhibits improved manufacturing yield and enhanced electrical isolation by leveraging the etch-rate differential to accommodate lithographic overlay tolerances. The self-aligned architecture permits aggressive scaling of gate-to-contact spacing while maintaining reliable dielectric isolation, thereby improving parasitic capacitance characteristics and device reliability in advanced technology nodes.

# Patent Abstract

## Integrated Circuit Structure and Method for Forming a Protected Gate Contact Over an Active FET Region

**ABSTRACT**

An integrated circuit structure and method of fabrication are disclosed for forming a self-aligned, protected gate contact positioned over an active region of a field-effect transistor (FET). The structure includes a semiconductor substrate having an active region with source/drain regions disposed adjacent a gate structure. The gate structure comprises a gate electrode capped with a dielectric protective layer having an etch selectivity differing from that of an adjacent interlayer dielectric. A gate contact extends through the interlayer dielectric to electrically couple with the gate electrode directly above the active region, while the dielectric protective layer and dielectric sidewall spacers cooperatively insulate the gate contact from the source/drain regions and source/drain contacts, thereby preventing electrical shorting.

The method includes forming the gate structure over the active region, depositing the dielectric protective layer over the gate electrode, and forming source/drain contacts adjacent the gate structure. A contact opening is selectively etched through the interlayer dielectric to expose a portion of the gate electrode, wherein the etch selectivity of the protective layer and sidewall spacers confines the opening and maintains isolation from adjacent conductive features. A conductive material is deposited within the opening to define the gate contact. The disclosed structure reduces device footprint by permitting gate contact placement over the active region rather than requiring displacement to an isolation region, thereby increasing circuit density while maintaining reliable electrical isolation.
